q: The concept of ‘Universal Banking’ was implemented in India on the recommendations of which committee?
explain: Universal Banking came to India following the R H Khan Committee recommendations.

q: The external advisory committee that reported to the RBI on the first-ever niche banking licence award process was headed by:
explain: The advisory committee on niche banks (payments banks and small finance banks) was headed by Nachiket Mor.

q: Which of the following statements about the FSLRC is NOT correct?
options: It reviews, simplifies and rewrites the laws affecting financial markets in India
It evolves a common set of principles for governance of financial sector regulatory institutions
It streamlines the regulatory architecture of financial markets
explain: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was formed in 2011, not 2013. The other three statements describe its work correctly.

q: The U K Sinha Committee was constituted for which area?
options: RBI panel on Rural Banks reforms
RBI panel on Payment Banks reforms
explain: Upendra Kumar Sinha headed the expert committee on MSMEs; it also recommended video KYC.

q: RBI formed a committee to review the regulatory and supervisory framework for Core Investment Companies (CICs). Who headed it?
explain: The CIC review committee was headed by Tapan Ray, as per the answer key of the SBI Clerk Main 2019 paper.

q: The 11-member committee headed by former Finance Secretary Ratan P Watal was related to which subject?
options: Incentivising transactions through cards and digital means
Indo-Pakistani war and the Simla Agreement
explain: The Watal Committee dealt with boosting digital payments by incentivising card and digital transactions.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recommendation of the Narasimham Committee, 1991?
options: Reduction of the capital adequacy ratio
explain: Narasimham I wanted capital adequacy to be strengthened, not reduced. The other three are among its recommendations.

q: Which committee recommended the formation of Debt Recovery Tribunals?
explain: Debt Recovery Tribunals (special tribunals to cut the time taken to settle recovery cases) came from the Narasimham Committee.

q: Which committee recommended Income Recognition and Asset Classification norms for banks?
explain: Income recognition and asset classification norms trace back to the Narasimham Committee on the financial system.

q: The Khan Commission, set up in 2004, was meant to:
options: Prepare a report on financial inclusion
Review the financial status of public sector banks
explain: The Khan panel of 2004 looked at financial inclusion, the same theme later taken up by Rangarajan (2006) and Nachiket Mor (2013).

q: The Committee on Financial Inclusion headed by Dr C Rangarajan was set up in:
explain: Rangarajan’s Committee on Financial Inclusion was set up in 2006, two years after the 2004 Khan report.

q: Which committee suggested initiatives on the ‘Medium-term Path on Financial Inclusion’?
explain: The medium-term path on financial inclusion is linked to the Deepak Mohanty Committee.

q: According to the Nachiket Mor Committee, every adult should have a bank account by:
explain: Mor recommended that every adult (above 18 years) get an account, the Universal Electronic Bank Account, by 1 January 2016.

q: On whose recommendations was NABARD established?
explain: The Shivaraman Committee recommended a dedicated agricultural and rural development bank, leading to NABARD.

q: Statement I: The Tarun Ramadorai Committee was set up to study various facets of household finance in India. Statement II: It evaluates households’ demand in financial markets for assets such as pensions as well as liabilities. Which is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II
explain: Both statements describe the Ramadorai Committee’s remit on household finance.

q: Which committee was formed to review the governance of boards of banks in India?
explain: The Nayak Committee examined the governance of boards of banks. Ghosh dealt with frauds and Eradi with insolvency law.

q: The Narasimham Committee I recommended a gradual reduction of the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) to:
explain: SLR was to be reduced gradually to 25%, and CRR to 3.5%.

q: Narasimham Committee I suggested bringing the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) down gradually to:
explain: The first committee suggested CRR of 3.5% and SLR of 25%.

q: Narasimham Committee I was set up in:
explain: The first committee began in August 1991, the year of economic liberalisation.

q: When was the Narasimham Committee II set up?
explain: Committee II was set up on 26 December 1997 and submitted its report in April 1998.

q: Which concept, recommended by the Narasimham Committee II, lets weak banks place their funds only in short-term, risk-free assets?
explain: Narrow Banking was the 1998 committee’s idea for weak banks.

q: The Narasimham Committee II looked at a stronger banking system in the context of which convertibility?
explain: The committee linked the banking system’s strength with Current Account Convertibility (CAC). Capital account convertibility is the tempting but wrong choice.

q: Which of these was recommended by the Narasimham Committee II (1998)?
options: Increasing the number of public sector banks
Raising the prescribed capital adequacy norms
explain: The 1998 committee wanted capital adequacy norms raised and an urgent review of banking-sector laws.

q: According to the Narasimham Committee I, Regional Rural Banks should focus on:
explain: The committee said RRBs should concentrate on agriculture and rural financing.

q: The Damodaran Committee of 2011 was headed by a former chairman of which body?
explain: M. Damodaran, a former SEBI Chairman, headed the committee set up by the RBI.

q: What was the Damodaran Committee asked to study?
options: Customer services and the grievance redressal mechanism in banks
explain: Its task was customer service and evaluating banks’ grievance redressal systems.

q: Which committee recommended No Frill Savings Accounts without any minimum balance?
explain: The Damodaran Committee asked banks to offer no-frill accounts with a cheque book and ATM card and no minimum balance.

q: Under the Damodaran Committee’s recommendation, the customer’s liability for losses in ATM and online transactions should be:
explain: The committee recommended that customers bear no liability for such losses.

q: The Usha Thorat Committee (2011) recommended a higher capital norm for NBFCs of:
explain: A 12% capital norm, plus asset classification and provisioning like banks, was proposed for NBFCs.

q: As per the Usha Thorat Committee, the minimum asset size to register a new NBFC is over:
explain: The committee suggested a minimum asset size of over ₹50 crore to register a new NBFC. The ₹1,000 crore figure is the exemption limit.

q: The Usha Thorat Committee exempted NBFCs not accessing public funds and having assets below:
explain: NBFCs that do not access public funds and hold assets below ₹1,000 crore were to be exempt from registration.

q: The M V Nair Committee of 2011 was set up to re-examine guidelines on:
explain: The Nair Committee revised the classification and guidelines for priority sector lending.

q: The M V Nair Committee was constituted following an announcement in which document?
explain: The committee was set up on 25 August 2011 pursuant to an announcement in the Monetary Policy Statement 2011-12.

q: What is the full form of UEBA, recommended by the Nachiket Mor Committee?
explain: UEBA stands for Universal Electronic Bank Account, proposed for every adult above 18 years.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee suggested abolishing which ratio gradually and bringing in the Liquidity Coverage Ratio?
explain: Mor proposed phasing out SLR and introducing LCR under Basel III norms.

q: Which kind of bank did the Nachiket Mor Committee recommend setting up?
explain: The 2013 committee recommended payments banks among its measures for inclusion.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee suggested that a bank issue an account to every resident at the time the person receives:
explain: The report linked account opening to the issue of the Aadhaar number (UIDAI).

q: Which committee recommended replacing the current KYC methods with video KYC?
explain: The expert MSME committee headed by U K Sinha recommended video KYC.

q: As per the RBI’s KYC guidelines, how often must KYC be completed for high-risk customers?
explain: High risk: 2 years; medium risk: 8 years; low risk: 10 years.

q: Under the RBI KYC guidelines, how often must KYC be refreshed for low-risk customers?
explain: Low-risk customers need KYC only once in 10 years.

q: Which pairing of customer risk level and KYC refresh interval is correct?
explain: The gaps are 2 years (high), 8 years (medium) and 10 years (low).

q: Which statement about video KYC is correct?
options: It requires a physical visit to the branch
It can only be done at an ATM
Documents are verified and the signature recorded during a video call with a bank officer
It is available only to NRIs
explain: Video KYC removes the need to visit a branch; it is completed in minutes over a video call.

q: On 5 May 2021, because of the COVID-19 pandemic, the RBI allowed:
options: Abolition of KYC for all accounts
Conversion of limited KYC accounts to full KYC accounts
Only physical KYC for small businesses
explain: RBI relaxed KYC norms: limited KYC accounts could be converted to full KYC, and video KYC was allowed for small businesses and legal entities.

q: The V G Kannan Committee was constituted for:
options: ATM charges and rural penetration of teller machines
explain: Kannan looked at ATM charges and improving rural penetration of ATMs.

q: The Nandan Nilekani Committee was set up for:
options: Strengthening the safety and security of digital payments
explain: The Nilekani panel’s objective was the safety and security of digital payments.

q: The A Ghosh Committee dealt with:
explain: Ghosh’s committee examined frauds and malpractices.

q: The R V Easwar Committee was formed to:
explain: Easwar’s task was simplifying the Income Tax Act, 1961.

q: The Parthasarathi Shome Committee gave guidelines on:
explain: Shome’s committee dealt with the General Anti Avoidance Rules (GAAR).

q: The Bimal Jalan Committee was constituted to:
options: Scrutinise applications for new bank licences
explain: Jalan’s panel scrutinised applications for new bank licences.

q: Which committee examined the current monetary policy framework?
explain: Urjit Patel reviewed the monetary policy framework; Vaghul dealt with the money market.

q: The Balakrishna Eradi Committee is associated with:
explain: Eradi’s panel looked at insolvency law.

q: The Wanchoo Committee examined:
explain: Wanchoo is listed with direct taxes enquiry; L K Jha and Rekhi with indirect taxes.

q: Which committee dealt with the ‘follow-up of bank credit’?
explain: Tandon is linked with the follow-up of bank credit; I T Vaz with working capital finance.

q: The R N Malhotra Committee recommended reforms in:
explain: Malhotra is associated with insurance sector reforms.

q: The Shyamala Gopinath Committee made suggestions on:
explain: Gopinath is linked with post office small saving schemes.

q: The Khusro Committee looked into:
explain: Khusro’s panel dealt with agricultural credit; Lakdawala handled the poverty line.

q: The Vaghul Committee recommended steps for the:
explain: Vaghul is associated with the money market.
